body: what is `$some_value` in your case? if it is an array it will create IN condition. If it is null it should generate correct SQL `somefield IS NULL`.

@cebe No, problem is step deeper, then SomeModel array is in place and Yii2 starts to populate relation. `other_model_uuid` can be either UUID or NULL, so it makes query: `SELECT * FROM tbl_some_other_model WHERE key IN(UUID,NULL)`, and this crashes. I need to find way to either filter off the NULL from relation array, or return all-zeroes UUID.
Ah, I guess nulls should not end in the criteria at all.
@samdark I agree, but where to hook in and bite them out ?

As `IN (0,1,2,NULL)` is valid SQL and array_filter will also remove the 0 from that list the solution is not complete and also only valid for the casandra implementation. It should go into a subclass though.
@cebe is `IN (0,1,2,NULL)` valid considering context of getting related records by PK?

Aha, `IN(0,NULL)` is a valid point, maybe better filter ?

OFFTOPIC: Did th Yii2 architect think of Dependency Injection ? ActiveRelation is instantiated 2 times in ActiveRecord, have to override both, but what if original methods will silently change so i will have to change my overides but will not be notified ?

@samdark at least the 0 is valid.

How does the NULL value come in there at least? Where did you tell yii that it can be NULL or UUID?

> OFFTOPIC: Did th Yii2 architect think of Dependency Injection ? ActiveRelation is instantiated 2 times in ActiveRecord, have to override both, but what if original methods will silently change so i will have to change my overides but will not be notified ?

For ActiveQuery we have a method that creates an instance which you can override to add yours.
For ActiveRelation there was no need to it yet and there will only be those two places as far as I see as they are shortcut methods for defining relations.

@cebe `0` is no doubt valid.

@mcd-php yes, we've considered "inject everything" approach. The only benefit at that time was ability to test things easier. The con was spoiling end user API so we went for good API. Architecture isn't finalized though, we're open to suggestions.

Maybe, `$values = array_filter($values,function($i){return $i!==null;});` ? 
Yii2 requires PHP >=5.3.7, so lambdas are fine.

NULL's come from junction tables, of course. See:

``` php
$arWorkersViaPositions = JobPosition::find()
    ->with('obWorker')
    ->where(array(
        'department' => $departmentId,
    ))
    ->all();
```

Job positions have full right to be vacant ( `$obJobPosition->worker = null; // Lazy moron fired` ) but not deleted, since they retain messages, tasks etc.

This way, if our department has vacancies, `SELECT * FROM user WHERE id IN ()` will have nulls.
@samdark So we found another benefit of injection - make framework use user-programmer's subclases by change in one point, namely the config of injector.

So we have 2 poins there:
1. In this concrete case there should be a single place to configure ActiveRelation via ActiveRecord. Either config or getter will do.
2. Nulls should be filtered out from `IN` case when getting relations.

@yiisoft/core-developers thoughts?
